summary: Phase 1 contract for mo-execute-and-fulfill — the EXECUTION half of the manufacturing-order lifecycle (pick → output → complete, plus batch start/complete and output-allocation routing) and the downstream sales-shipment fulfillment that consumes from MO-produced lots through stock_allocations buckets. SO↔MO link creation and shipment-cost margin entries are in scope only insofar as they touch this surface. The feature is a composite of three server-side DAL entry points (manufacturing/queries.ts, sales/queries.ts, inventory kernel) plus their HTTP routes. The UI surface is `/manufacturing/orders/[id]/execute` (manufacturing-execution.tsx) and the shipment dialogs on the sales order detail. Every business rule listed below is grounded in a code citation with a confidence tag.

inferences: Because CLAUDE.md describes `recomputeExpectedQty` as the conceptual contract but the code uses event-driven `applyExpectedReferenceDeltasInTx` deltas (addExpectedFromManufacturingInTx on release, editExpectedFromManufacturingInTx on plan edit, produceManufacturedStockInTx + releaseRemainingExpectedOutputInTx on output/complete), Rule 5 is best expressed as 'expected supply lifecycle is event-driven via subtypes manufacturing_release / manufacturing_edit / manufacturing_complete' rather than a literal function call.

Because each batch completion calls produceManufacturedStockInTx without passing a lotId (queries.ts 6095-6108), each completed batch produces ONE new lot via createPositiveStockEventInTx. Multiple discrete /outputs calls on the same MO instead reuse getProducedLotIdInTx and append via appendPositiveStockToExistingLotInTx. The batch path therefore guarantees the 'one lot per batch' invariant; the discrete /outputs path collapses to one lot for the whole order.

Because completeManufacturingOrder explicitly rejects manufacturingMode='batch' (5545-5550) and completeManufacturingBatch explicitly rejects manufacturingMode='discrete' (5866-5868), the two paths are mutually exclusive at the API surface — clients must dispatch on mode.

Because cancelReleasedManufacturingOrderInTx is reached via the DELETE route (no Idempotency-Key required) but uses a deterministic internal key 'delete-manufacturing-order:<order.id>' (queries.ts 6807), repeated DELETEs do replay safely server-side even though no client header is enforced.

Because updateSalesShipmentCosts hard-deletes all costs and re-inserts the supplied set (6957-6976), the endpoint is idempotent-in-effect even without Idempotency-Key enforcement. Cost edits cannot mutate inventory, AP, GL, BOL state, or Xero invoices.
unknowns: Whether discrete /outputs that consume more than one batch's worth of pre-picked stock interact correctly when the order also has variance reconciliation at /complete (out-of-scope for this contract because batch-mode /outputs is rejected for discrete and discrete /outputs is allowed only when manufacturingMode='discrete').
Whether saveManufacturingOutputAllocation racing with shipSalesShipment leads to a deterministic outcome — the route is not wrapped in beginInventoryOperationInTx and not Idempotency-Key gated.

Whether output adjust-down (negative /outputs) on a batch-mode MO re-shrinks the produced batch lot or just zeroes the output row; reverseManufacturingOutputInTx was not opened line-by-line in this phase.

structured_output.purpose: Drive a released manufacturing order from picked ingredients through produced output to a completed/closed state, propagate produced supply into downstream sales shipments via stock allocations, and ship the sales shipment lines while preserving inventory ledger integrity, weighted-average cost, and idempotent replay.
structured_output.domain_role: Execution layer of the manufacturing module. The release step writes demand and expected supply but does NOT consume stock. Picking, output recording, and completion are the stock-affecting steps. On the sales side, ship is the stock-affecting step; cost edits are margin-only. Stock allocations are the bridge that lets an MO promise specific output capacity to a sales order line or shipment line, materialising into concrete lot holds at produce time.

Allocation bucket: 'sales_order_line' for unplanned residual demand; 'sales_shipment_line' for planned shipment-line demand. Materialised MO output appears as 'inventory_lot' source against whichever demand still has open qty.

user_actions: Start batch (batch-mode only): transitions current batch from 'pending' to 'in_progress' and stamps startedAt.

Mark ingredient done (pick): consumes the ingredient's full remaining planned quantity from held holds first, then FIFO; writes manufacturing_pick_allocations; ingredients[i].pickStatus -> 'picked'; batch row pickedAt stamped if every batch ingredient fully picked.
Confirm pick over lot-age requirement: re-issue pick with confirmRequirementOverride=true to bypass minimum lot age.
Confirm pick into negative stock: re-issue pick with confirmNegativeStock=true (also acts as requirement override).

Record output (discrete or batch): inserts manufacturing_order_outputs row; on first call creates the produced lot, on subsequent calls appends to the same lot via weighted-average cost; outputDisposition controls whether the lot materialises MO source allocations.
Reverse output: POST /outputs with negative quantity; reverseManufacturingOutputInTx walks the consumption rows back.

Complete order (discrete): if output already recorded, just releases remaining reservations + expected supply and flips status='done'; otherwise produces the output lot from picked stock, optionally reconciling ingredient actuals via reconcileIngredientActualsInTx, then flips status='done'.
Complete batch (batch-mode): completes the current batch (assertCurrentExecutionBatch), creates one new lot, stamps manufacturingOrderBatches.lotId. Parent MO flips to 'done' only when allCompleted.

Save output allocation: redirect a released MO's promised output across sales_order_line and manufacturing_order_ingredient demands; if output already exists, immediately materialises promises into the produced lot.

Cancel manufacturing order: DELETE /[id] soft-deletes the order; cancelReleasedManufacturingOrderInTx unpicks any picked ingredients, releases reservations + expected supply, cancels all stock_allocations sourced from this MO or demanded by this MO's ingredients.
Plan a sales shipment (out of scope here but the bucket transition matters): pulls unplanned sales_order_line allocations into the new sales_shipment_line via moveActiveSalesAllocationsInTx.
Delete a sales shipment: cancelShipmentLineAllocationsInTx moves allocations back to the sales_order_line bucket.

Ship a planned shipment: consumeForShipmentInTx consumes inventory_lot holds first, falls through to FIFO if eligible, throws InsufficientStockError before FIFO if a manufacturing_order promise is still open on the shipment line; transitions shipment to 'shipped' and flips parent order to 'done' when all lines closed.

Confirm ship into negative stock: re-issue ship with confirmNegativeStock=true; consumeForShipmentInTx falls through to consumeStockFifoInTx with allowNegativeStock=true and creates a NEG-* synthetic lot.
Edit shipment costs: PUT /costs replaces the cost rows; never mutates inventory or accounting state.

Three distinct 409 surfaces (pick stock_shortage, pick requirement_violation, ship negativeStock) with three override flags. Tests must read the correct discriminator from the response body and retry with the correct flag (and trust testFetch to derive a new Idempotency-Key from the changed body).

Cost basis cycles: a circular product BOM throws MissingCostBasisError(reason='product_bom_cost') deep inside produceManufacturedStockInTx; routes only catch InsufficientStockError and ManufacturingError, so this becomes a 500 surfaces. Tests that exercise product BOMs should assert no cycle.

Batch-mode partial-completion expected supply: intermediate batches release only their slice; final batch releases all remaining expected. Mis-accounting could leave a residual expected_increase that never releases.

Discrete /outputs producing into a single lot via appendPositiveStockToExistingLotInTx weighted-averages cost; if /complete later supplies ingredient variance, the lot's unitCost is computed only from the first output's snapshot, while manufacturing_orders.actualCostPerUnit is computed from variance-adjusted totals — divergence between the lot row and the order row.
/output-allocation PUT is not Idempotency-Key gated and not wrapped in beginInventoryOperationInTx. Concurrent edits or concurrent /ship of the same shipment line race.

consumeForShipmentInTx refuses fall-through when a manufacturing_order promise is still open on the shipment line. A shipment line carrying BOTH 'inventory_lot' AND 'manufacturing_order' source allocations consumes the lot portion first, then 409s on the rest — partial state must be inspected carefully.

Xero push side-effect runs OUTSIDE the inventory transaction; idempotency replay of the inventory portion does NOT re-fire the Xero push. Tests asserting Xero outbox effects must account for this asymmetry.

MO soft-delete (DELETE /[id]) is the de-facto cancel and is not Idempotency-Key gated by route; it relies on an internal deterministic key. Repeated DELETE calls are safe server-side but clients still get a 404 on the second attempt because the order is already deletedAt.
Output disposition='blocked' bypasses materialisation; a downstream sales shipment that expected to pull from this MO will then 409 at ship time even though the lot exists.

Negative-stock NEG-<date>-<uuid> lots: shipping into negative stock requires resolvePositiveStockUnitCostInTx to succeed (BR-4); a product without an active BOM that ships into negative stock surfaces MissingCostBasisError as a 500.
